test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In a 2100 m circular race, Amit finishes one round in 42 seconds and Sumit finishes one round in 75 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **time taken** by Amit and Sumit to complete one round = 42 : 75 = 14 : 25.

Since **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**, Ratio of **speeds** (u : v) = 25 : 14.

For **opposite directions**, Number of **distinct meeting points** = u + v.

Number of meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f727ed306389e418b547665a2b1c7d04282eb26753ce525182e638f4d99805af.png] 

**Given:** Track Length = 2100 m, TAₘᵢₜ = 42 s, TSᵤₘᵢₜ = 75 s.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Distinct points (opposite) = Ratio of speeds (a + b) where a/b is in simplest form.

⇒ Speed of Amit (SA) = 2100 ÷ 42 = 50 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sumit (SS) = 2100 ÷ 75 = 28 m/s

⇒ Ratio of Speeds SA : SS = 50 : 28

⇒ Simplest Ratio = 25 : 14

⇒ Number of distinct meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Points in Same Direction

If two people run in the **same direction** with speeds in the simplest ratio a : b (a > b), the number of distinct meeting points is (a − b).

Time of First Meeting

The time taken for the **first meeting anywhere** on the track is Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Time of Meeting at Starting Point

The time when they meet for the first time at the **starting point** is the LCM of the time taken by each to complete one full round.</p
